transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because... I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer for work, or, you know, trying to relax after dinner, I just have this tension I can't shake.
How long have you been feeling this constant tension? Has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?
I'd say it's been going on for months... actually, about thirteen months now. It started right around the time my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family.
When you feel this tension and feel wound up, do you find yourself worrying a lot about specific things, or does the worry seem to come up about many different topics?

Well, it's really a lot of different topics. My mind just... it keeps going from one concern to another. 

I'll be thinking about my sister in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm worrying about whether I missed something at the office. Then it shifts to my husband driving home, or my church commitments, or paying the bills. It just doesn't stop. I always find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet.
On most days when you're experiencing this worry and tension, how much does it interfere with your ability to concentrate at work or handle your daily responsibilities?

Well, I'm still getting my work done, and I'm still showing up for my family and my church commitments. But... it definitely takes a toll. It takes me a lot longer to finish my reports at work because I find myself double-checking things way more than I used to. And at home, I've had to apologize a few times lately because I end up sounding a bit short with my husband and the people I care about. So, I'm managing, but it's just harder than it should be.
Besides the mental tension you've described, do you notice physical symptoms? For example, do you experience muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or feeling unusually tired?

Well, sleep is definitely a problem. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but then... I wake up around three or four in the morning. My mind just starts going, thinking about my sister’s next appointment or some server issue at work. And because of that, even when I technically get enough hours of sleep, I start the morning feeling like I never really rested.
You mentioned feeling wound up and tense in your body. When you experience that physical tension, do you notice your muscles feeling tight or knotted, particularly in your neck, shoulders, or jaw?

I don't really think so. I haven't noticed any knots or tightness in my neck or jaw. I mean, I sit at a computer for my job, so I get a little stiff sometimes just from staring at the screen all day, but... no, I wouldn't say my muscles feel tight or painful from being wound up. It's more just an overall feeling of being on edge.
When you feel that sense of being on edge, do you find yourself having difficulty sitting still? For example, do you feel restless or have an urge to move around?

Honestly, that's actually why I came in to see someone. I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's not necessarily that I have to get up and pace around the room, but... it feels like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer for work, or trying to relax after dinner, I have that feeling. I just can't seem to fully settle down.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where your anxiety or sense of being on edge suddenly intensifies quite a bit, where you might notice your heart racing, sweating, or difficulty breathing—even if nothing particularly stressful is happening at that moment?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. It doesn't suddenly spike out of nowhere with my heart racing or anything. It's more of just a constant, steady feeling of being on edge, rather than a sudden attack.
You mentioned sounding short with your husband and others lately. Beyond just being short, do you find yourself feeling irritable or having a shorter temper than you normally would?

Yeah, I think so. I'm usually a pretty patient person, but lately... I don't know, just little things seem to get to me. Like at work, if someone is late with an update in a documentation meeting, or at choir practice if someone is singing off-tempo. Even on Sundays when I'm cooking, if my husband or anyone asks me too many questions, I just... I find myself answering a lot sharper than I mean to. It's like I just have a shorter fuse right now.

When you're trying to focus on something—like reading an email or working on a report—do you find it hard to keep your attention on that one task because your mind keeps jumping to these different worries?

Yes, that happens a lot. I'll be trying to work, and I'll tell myself, 'Daniela, enough, just focus on this report.' But then one small thought pops up, and that turns into five more. Before I even realize it, I've spent half an hour just checking messages or replaying everything that could possibly go wrong instead of actually getting my work done. It's really hard to stop it once it starts.
Have you had any episodes where you suddenly feel a wave of intense fear or anxiety that builds up quickly over a few minutes, even when you're not in an obviously dangerous or stressful situation?

No, I think that's similar to what you asked a few minutes ago. I don't really get those sudden waves of intense fear. It doesn't build up quickly like that for me. Like I mentioned, it's really just more of a constant, steady worry that's always kind of there in the background.
